mainTopic: The ברכת אבלים and the ten-man quorum, the story of ריש לקיש's comfort blessings, and the customs of the house of mourning (ten cups, רבן גמליאל's simple burials).
overview: The גמרא first settles where רבי יוחנן's rule applies: mourners are not counted in a quorum of ten. It moves the rule from the שורה, the line of comforters, to the רחבה, where the ברכת אבלים is said. It then explains that this blessing can be said all seven days when פנים חדשות, new visitors, arrive. To show this, it tells how ריש לקיש came on the second day to comfort רב חייא בר אבא, whose child had died. ריש לקיש's spokesman spoke about the child, and the גמרא explains that his harsh-sounding words were really an honor. The spokesman then said four blessings: praise of הקב"ה, comfort for the mourners, a blessing for the comforters, and a prayer for all ישראל. Along the way, אביי teaches not to speak of future deaths, because one should never 'open his mouth to the שטן.' Finally the גמרא lists the ten cups of wine set up for the house of mourning, and explains the cup once added for רבן גמליאל, who made burials simple and cheap. A new statement of רבי אלעזר begins at the end and continues on the next amud.

steps.title: The ברייתא is about ברכת המזון; רבי יוחנן is about the line of comforters
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא resolves the contradiction by giving each source a different setting. A mourner counts for ברכת המזון, but not for the ten men in the שורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: When that ברייתא was taught, it was about ברכת המזון. When רבי יוחנן spoke, he was talking about the line of comforters.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the contradiction between רבי יוחנן and the ברייתא by saying they are talking about two different situations.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ברייתא, which counts a mourner, is about the group needed to say ברכת המזון together. A mourner must say ברכת המזון himself, so he can join. רבי יוחנן's rule, that mourners are not counted, is about the שורה, the ten men who stand in a line to comfort the mourners after the burial.

keyTerms.meaning: The line of comforters formed after a burial
When he said it, he was talking about...

phrases.english: When that [ברייתא] was taught, it was about Grace after Meals,
phrases.notes: "That ברייתא" is the one from just before this, which seemed to count a mourner.

phrases.english: when Rabbi Yochanan said [mourners are not counted], it was about the line.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the contradiction raised just before this section, between רבי יוחנן and the ברייתא.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Different settings: each source is about a different kind of quorum.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: Both sources seemed to be about the same quorum of ten, so they seemed to contradict each other.
steps.terutzMaskana: The ברייתא is about ברכת המזון and רבי יוחנן is about the שורה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן's rule mentions a blessing, and there is no blessing in the line
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a fuller version of רבי יוחנן's statement. It talks about a 'blessing of the mourners,' but no blessing is said in the שורה.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the grooms' blessing is said with ten, and the grooms count. The mourners' blessing is said with ten, and the mourners do not count. Is there any blessing said in the line?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא challenges the answer from Step 1 by quoting רבי יוחנן's exact words.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבי יוחנן's statement is about a ברכת אבלים, a blessing for mourners that needs ten men. In the שורה, people just stand and comfort the mourners; no blessing is said there. So Step 1's answer cannot fit רבי יוחנן's words.

keyTerms.meaning: The blessing of the grooms (שבע ברכות)
The blessing said to comfort mourners
Counted in the tally of ten

steps.confusionAlert: Grooms DO count toward the ten, but mourners do NOT. Don't mix up the two halves of the statement.

phrases.english: But then, that which Rabbi Yitzchak said
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:
We say the blessing of the grooms with ten,
and the grooms are counted in the tally.
And the blessing of the mourners is with ten,
and the mourners are not counted in the tally.
Is there a blessing in the line?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Attacks Step 1's claim that רבי יוחנן was talking about the שורה.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in Step 1 that רבי יוחנן's rule applies to the שורה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן's own words mention a blessing, and no blessing is said in the שורה.

steps.title: רבי יוחנן was talking about the square
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא changes its answer: רבי יוחנן's rule is about the רחבה, the square where the mourners' blessing is said.
steps.simpleTranslation: Rather, when רבי יוחנן said this, he was talking about the square.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a new setting for רבי יוחנן's rule, one where a blessing really is said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the רחבה, the square near the cemetery, a meal and blessings for the mourners took place. That fits the words 'blessing of the mourners.' There ten men are needed, and the mourners do not count among them.

keyTerms.meaning: The open square where the mourners' blessing was said

phrases.english: Rather, when Rabbi Yochanan said [this],
it was about the square.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Replaces the 'line' answer from Step 1 with the 'square' answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Changes the setting to one where a blessing is said.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: רבי יוחנן was talking about the שורה.
steps.terutzMaskana: רבי יוחנן was talking about the רחבה, where the ברכת אבלים is said.

steps.title: The blessing is said all seven days, but the square is only on the first day
steps.stepSummary: Another version of רבי יוחנן's statement says the blessings are said 'all seven days.' But the gathering in the רחבה happens only right after the burial.
steps.simpleTranslation: But what about what רבי יצחק said in the name of רבי יוחנן: the grooms' blessing is said with ten all seven days, and the grooms count. The mourners' blessing is said with ten all seven days, and the mourners do not count. Is there a blessing in the square all seven days?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא attacks the 'square' answer from Step 3, using a version of רבי יוחנן's words that says the blessing is said for seven days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The meal and blessing in the רחבה happen once, right after the burial. If רבי יוחנן says the mourners' blessing is said for all seven days, it doesn't seem to fit the רחבה.

keyTerms.meaning: All seven days (of the wedding celebration, or of mourning)

phrases.english: But then, that which Rabbi Yitzchak said
in the name of Rabbi Yochanan:

phrases.aramaic: מְבָרְכִין בִּרְכַּת חֲתָנִים בַּעֲשָׂרָה כׇּל שִׁבְעָה,
phrases.english: We say the blessing of the grooms with ten all seven days,
and the grooms are counted in the tally.
And the blessing of the mourners is with ten all seven days,
and the mourners are not counted in the tally.

phrases.aramaic: בִּרְכַּת רְחָבָה כׇּל שִׁבְעָה מִי אִיכָּא?
phrases.english: Is there a blessing of the square all seven days?

steps.triggerLanguage: וְאֶלָּא הָא דְּאָמַר רַבִּי יִצְחָק אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the 'square' answer from Step 3.
steps.kashyaTarget: The answer in Step 3 that רבי יוחנן's rule applies to the רחבה.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: רבי יוחנן says 'all seven days,' but the blessing in the רחבה is said only once, after the burial.

steps.title: It happens when new visitors come
steps.stepSummary: The blessing can be said later in the שבעה when פנים חדשות, people who were not there before, come to comfort the mourners.
steps.simpleTranslation: You can find it when new faces come.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא defends the 'square' answer by showing how the mourners' blessing can be said again during the seven days.
steps.deeperAnalysis: When new people who were not at the burial arrive, the words of comfort and the ברכת אבלים are said again. So the blessing can be said on any of the seven days, and the 'square' answer still works.

keyTerms.meaning: You can find it (a case where it happens)
New faces: people who were not there before

steps.whatToRemember: Final picture: mourners do not count toward the ten for ברכת אבלים. That blessing is said in the רחבה after the burial, and again during the שבעה whenever פנים חדשות come.

phrases.english: You find it with new faces.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the challenge of Step 4 and keeps the 'square' answer.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Gives a case where the blessing is said again later.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The ברכת אבלים is only said once, right after the burial.
steps.terutzMaskana: It is said again during the שבעה whenever פנים חדשות arrive.

steps.title: ריש לקיש goes to comfort רב חייא בר אבא
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא begins a story about words of comfort said to a mourner. רב חייא בר אבא, a teacher of ריש לקיש's children, lost a child, and ריש לקיש came on the second day.
steps.simpleTranslation: Like the story of רב חייא בר אבא, who taught תנ"ך to ריש לקיש's sons. Some say he taught משנה to ריש לקיש's son. A child of his died. On the first day ריש לקיש did not go to him. The next day he took along יהודה בר נחמני, his spokesman.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא starts a story about comforting a mourner. This step sets the scene for the words of comfort in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story backs up the answer about פנים חדשות. ריש לקיש did not come on the first day but on the next day, so he is a new face, and the blessings for the mourners are said again for him (steps 13-19).

keyTerms.meaning: Spokesman who repeated a רבי's words aloud to the crowd

phrases.aramaic: כִּי הָא דְּרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
phrases.english: Like that [story] of Rav Chiya bar Abba,
he was the Bible teacher of Reish Lakish's sons,

phrases.aramaic: וְאָמְרִי לַהּ מַתְנִי בְּרֵיהּ דְּרֵישׁ לָקִישׁ הֲוָה.
phrases.english: and some say he was the Mishnah teacher of Reish Lakish's son.
A child of his died.
phrases.notes: "His" means רב חייא בר אבא's child.

phrases.english: On the first day, [Reish Lakish] did not go to him.

phrases.aramaic: לִמְחַר דַּבְרֵיהּ לִיהוּדָה בַּר נַחְמָנִי מְתוּרְגְּמָנֵיהּ.
phrases.english: The next day he took Yehuda bar Nachmani, his spokesman, [with him].

steps.triggerLanguage: כִּי הָא דְּרַב חִיָּיא בַּר אַבָּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Illustrates the answer of step 5: a new visitor (ריש לקיש, on the second day) comes, and blessings for the mourners are recited.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Sets up a story: ריש לקיש comes on the second day, with his spokesman, to comfort רב חייא בר אבא.
steps.raayaObject: Step 5's answer that the ברכת אבלים is said again during the שבעה when פנים חדשות arrive.
steps.raayaSupportSource: The story of ריש לקיש comforting רב חייא בר אבא on the second day, with blessings recited.

steps.title: The spokesman opens with a פסוק about children dying
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks יהודה בר נחמני to say something about the child. He opens with a פסוק and explains that when fathers anger הקב"ה, their children die young.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to him: Get up and say something about the child. He began and said: 'And ה׳ saw and He abhorred, because of the anger of His sons and daughters.' A generation in which the fathers anger הקב"ה, He is angry at their sons and daughters, and they die while they are small.
steps.whatsHappening: The spokesman begins his words about the child's death with a דרשה on a פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: He reads the פסוק as saying that when the fathers of a generation anger הקב"ה, the punishment can fall on their young children. This is only the opening of his speech. Step 12 explains what he meant, and steps 13-19 bring the rest of his words.

keyTerms.meaning: A word or matter: here, words of comfort

steps.confusionAlert: This sounds harsh as comfort, and it is only the opening. The speech continues past this point, so don't treat this line as the whole message.

phrases.english: He said to him: Get up and say something
about the child.
He began and said:
"And the Lord saw and He abhorred,
phrases.notes: דברים 32:19

phrases.english: because of the anger of His sons and His daughters."

phrases.aramaic: דּוֹר שֶׁאָבוֹת מְנָאֲצִים לְהַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא —
phrases.english: A generation in which the fathers anger the Holy One, Blessed be He —
phrases.notes: He reads the word "וַיִּנְאָץ" as the fathers angering הקב"ה, which is why the sons and daughters are mentioned.

phrases.english: He is angry at their sons and at their daughters,
and they die while they are small.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: קוּם אֵימָא מִלְּתָא כׇּל קֳבֵיל יָנוֹקָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story. The spokesman begins the words of comfort.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: דרשה: when the fathers of a generation anger הקב"ה, their young children may die.

steps.title: Another version: the child was a young man
steps.stepSummary: According to another version, the child who died was a בחור, and יהודה בר נחמני quoted a פסוק from ישעיהו about young men dying because of the people's sins.
steps.simpleTranslation: Some say the child was a young man. In that version, יהודה בר נחמני quoted this פסוק: 'Therefore ה' will not rejoice over his young men, and He will not have mercy on his orphans and widows. Everyone is a flatterer and an evildoer, and every mouth speaks vulgar things. Even so, His anger has not turned back, and His hand is still stretched out.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives a second version of the story. In this version the child who died was older, and יהודה בר נחמני quoted a different פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first version (step 7), the child was young, and the פסוק was about children who die because their fathers angered הקב"ה. Here the child was a בחור, so the פסוק chosen talks about 'בחוריו,' young men. The message is the same: the sins of the people bring this kind of loss.

keyTerms.meaning: A young man, older than a small child
And His hand is still stretched out, meaning more punishment is still coming

phrases.english: And some say he was a young man.
phrases.notes: 'He' is the child of רב חייא בר אבא who died.

phrases.english: And this is what he said to him:

phrases.aramaic: ״עַל כֵּן עַל בַּחוּרָיו לֹא יִשְׂמַח ה׳
phrases.english: "Therefore the Lord will not rejoice over his young men,
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 9:16

phrases.aramaic: וְאֶת יְתוֹמָיו וְאֶת אַלְמְנוֹתָיו לֹא יְרַחֵם
phrases.english: and He will not have mercy on his orphans and his widows,
for everyone is a flatterer and an evildoer,
and every mouth speaks vulgar things.
Even so, His anger has not turned back,
and His hand is still stretched out."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a second version of the words said in step 7, using a different פסוק that matches an older child.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: In this version the child was a בחור, and the פסוק quoted is ישעיהו 9:16 about young men dying because of the people's sins.

steps.title: What does 'His hand is still stretched out' mean?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what the end of the פסוק, 'ועוד ידו נטויה,' is teaching.
steps.simpleTranslation: What does 'and His hand is still stretched out' mean?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא stops the story for a moment to ask about the last words of the פסוק. This sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק has already listed punishments, so the words 'His hand is still stretched out' seem to say that even more punishment is coming. The גמרא wants to know which sin causes that extra punishment.

keyTerms.meaning: What? Used to ask for the meaning of a word or phrase

phrases.english: What is the meaning of "and His hand is still stretched out"?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks for the meaning of the last phrase of the פסוק quoted in step 8.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra punishment is meant by 'His hand is still stretched out,' and what causes it?

steps.title: Vulgar speech can turn a good decree into a bad one
steps.stepSummary: רב חנן בר רב explains that vulgar speech is so serious that it can turn even a decree of seventy good years into a bad decree.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב חנן בר רב said: Everyone knows why a bride goes under the חופה. But anyone who makes his mouth vulgar and says dirty words, even if a decree of seventy good years was sealed for him, it is turned against him for bad.
steps.whatsHappening: רב חנן בר רב answers the question. The 'stretched out hand' is the punishment for speaking vulgar words, which the פסוק mentions just before ('every mouth speaks vulgar things').
steps.deeperAnalysis: His example is that everyone knows what happens after a wedding, yet no one should talk about it in a vulgar way. The point is not that the topic is secret. Saying it crudely is the sin, and it is serious enough to turn a good decree into a bad one.

keyTerms.meaning: One who makes his mouth vulgar by speaking dirty words
A decree or sentence from Heaven

steps.confusionAlert: רב חנן בר רב is not saying it is wrong to know about marriage. Everyone knows. The sin is speaking about it in a crude, vulgar way.

phrases.english: Rav Ḥanan bar Rav said:
Everyone knows, about a bride,
why she goes under the wedding canopy.
But anyone who makes his mouth vulgar
and lets a dirty word come out of his mouth,
even if a decree was sealed for him
of seventy years for good,
it is turned against him for bad.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַב חָנָן בַּר רַב: הַכֹּל יוֹדְעִין כַּלָּה לָמָּה נִכְנְסָה לַחוּפָּה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 9 by tying the 'stretched out hand' to the sin of vulgar speech.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is a well-known statement about how serious נבול פה is. It can reverse even a good decree from Heaven.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The extra punishment comes because of נבול פה. Vulgar speech can turn a sealed decree of seventy good years into a bad one.

steps.title: He came to comfort, but he caused pain
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא challenges the story: יהודה בר נחמני came to comfort the mourner, yet his words seem to blame the father's sins for his son's death.
steps.simpleTranslation: He came to comfort him, and instead he is hurting him!
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא returns to the story and asks a sharp question. How can words that seem to blame the mourner count as comfort?
steps.deeperAnalysis: In both versions of the story (step 7 and step 8), the פסוק he quoted connects a child's death to sins. Saying this to a grieving father sounds like telling him the death was his fault, which is the opposite of comforting him.

phrases.english: He came to comfort him,
and he is causing him pain!

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Goes back to the story after the side explanation in steps 9-10 and challenges what יהודה בר נחמני said.
steps.kashyaTarget: The words of יהודה בר נחמני in steps 7-8, which link the child's death to sin.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Someone who comes to comfort should not say words that seem to blame the mourner for his loss.

steps.title: You are important enough to suffer for the generation
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains that he meant: you are so important that you are the one punished for the sins of the generation.
steps.simpleTranslation: This is what he was telling him: You are important enough to be taken because of the generation.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the challenge. The words were not blame. They were praise: the sins belong to the generation, and a great person like you suffers for them.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'fathers' and 'everyone' in the פסוקים are the whole generation, not רב חייא בר אבא himself. A righteous person is sometimes the one taken for the sins of everyone, so the words actually honor him.

keyTerms.meaning: To be seized, meaning to be punished or suffer

phrases.english: This is what he was saying to him:
You are important enough to be seized for the generation.
phrases.notes: He means you suffer because of the generation's sins, not your own.

steps.triggerLanguage: הָכִי קָאָמַר לֵיהּ: חֲשִׁיב אַתְּ לְאִתְּפוֹסֵי אַדָּרָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the קשיא of step 11 by explaining what the words really meant.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The words blamed רב חייא בר אבא's own sins for his child's death.
steps.terutzMaskana: The words honored him: he was important enough to suffer for the sins of the whole generation.

steps.title: Words in praise of הקב"ה
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks יהודה בר נחמני to say words praising הקב"ה, and he says a blessing that ends 'מחיה המתים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to him: Stand and say something about the praise of הקב"ה. He began and said: 'The God Who is great in His great greatness, mighty and strong in His many awesome deeds, Who brings the dead back to life with His word, Who does great things that cannot be understood and wonders that cannot be counted. Blessed are You, ה', Who brings the dead back to life.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues. ריש לקיש asks for words praising הקב"ה, and יהודה בר נחמני says a blessing about God's greatness and תחיית המתים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: After speaking about the child, the next part of the comfort is praising הקב"ה. The blessing focuses on תחיית המתים, which gives hope to the mourners that the dead will live again.

keyTerms.meaning: Who brings the dead back to life

phrases.english: He said to him: Stand and say something
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש is speaking to יהודה בר נחמני.

phrases.aramaic: כְּנֶגֶד שְׁבָחוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא. פָּתַח וְאָמַר:
phrases.english: about the praise of the Holy One, Blessed be He. He began and said:
"The God Who is great in His great greatness,
mighty and strong in His many awesome deeds,
Who brings the dead back to life with His word,
Who does great things that cannot be understood
and wonders that cannot be counted.
Blessed are You, Lord, Who brings the dead back to life."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: קוּם אֵימָא מִלְּתָא כְּנֶגֶד שְׁבָחוֹ שֶׁל הַקָּדוֹשׁ בָּרוּךְ הוּא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story: after the words about the child, ריש לקיש asks for words praising הקב"ה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words of praise are a blessing about God's greatness that ends 'ברוך אתה ה' מחיה המתים'.

steps.title: Words of comfort for the mourners
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks for words for the mourners, and יהודה בר נחמני says that death has been the path of all people since Creation, ending with 'ברוך מנחם אבלים'.
steps.simpleTranslation: ריש לקיש said to him: Stand and say something for the mourners. He began and said: 'Our brothers, who are worn out and crushed by this mourning, set your hearts to think about this. This is something that stays forever. It has been a path since the six days of Creation. Many have drunk, and many will drink. As the first ones drank, so the last ones will drink. Our brothers, may the Master of comfort comfort you. Blessed is He Who comforts mourners.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues with words spoken directly to the mourners. יהודה בר נחמני tells them that death is part of the world for everyone, and he blesses them with comfort from הקב"ה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The 'drinking' is the cup of death that every person tastes. The comfort is that this loss is not unusual or a sign that they were singled out, because it has been the way of the world since Creation. This blessing ends 'מנחם אבלים,' the kind of mourners' blessing discussed earlier in the סוגיא (steps 3-5).

keyTerms.meaning: Those who are worn out and tired
The Master of comfort, meaning הקב"ה

phrases.english: He said to him: Stand and say something
for the mourners. He began and said:
"Our brothers, who are worn out,
who are crushed by this mourning,
set your hearts to think about this.
This is something that stays forever.
It has been a path since the six days of Creation.
phrases.notes: 'It' is death. It has been part of the world from the very beginning.

phrases.english: Many have drunk, and many will drink.
phrases.notes: The 'drink' is the cup of death that every person tastes.

phrases.english: As the first ones drank, so the last ones will drink.
Our brothers, may the Master of comfort comfort you.
Blessed is He Who comforts mourners."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: קוּם אֵימָא מִלְּתָא כְּנֶגֶד אֲבֵלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story right after the praise of הקב"ה with the last part of the comfort, spoken to the mourners themselves.
steps.whyThisMatters: It gives an actual wording of a mourners' blessing ending 'מנחם אבלים,' which connects the story back to the earlier discussion of ברכת אבלים.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The words for the mourners teach that death has been the way of all people since Creation, and they end with the blessing 'ברוך מנחם אבלים'.

steps.title: אביי: Speak of Past Drinking, Not Future Drinking
steps.stepSummary: אביי rules that in the words of comfort one may say 'many have drunk' and 'the drink of the first ones,' but not 'many will drink' or 'the drink of the last ones.'
steps.simpleTranslation: אביי said: Saying 'Many have drunk' is fine. Saying 'Many will drink' is not. Saying 'The drink of the first ones' is fine. Saying 'The drink of the last ones' is not.
steps.whatsHappening: אביי comments on the wording of the comfort from the last step, where death is pictured as a cup that people drink. He says to talk only about people who already died, not about people who will die.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The idea that 'everyone drinks this cup' is fine to say about the past. But saying the same thing about the future sounds like you are predicting more deaths. So אביי cuts out the future part of the comfort.

keyTerms.meaning: He may say it / let him say it
A drink; here, the 'cup' of death
The earlier ones / the later ones

phrases.english: Abaye said:
"Many have drunk": let him say it.
phrases.notes: 'Drinking' here means dying, as if death were a cup that everyone must drink from.

phrases.english: "Many will drink": let him not say it.
"The drink of the first ones": let him say it.
"The drink of the last ones": let him not say it.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adjusts the wording of the comfort words said in step 14.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: When comforting, speak only of deaths that already happened, never of deaths still to come.

steps.title: Never Open Your Mouth to the שטן
steps.stepSummary: The reason for אביי's rule: רבי שמעון בן לקיש, and a teaching in the name of רבי יוסי, say a person should never 'open his mouth to the שטן.'
steps.simpleTranslation: This is like רבי שמעון בן לקיש said, and the same was taught in the name of רבי יוסי: A person should never open his mouth to the שטן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives the source and reason behind אביי's rule.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Talking about bad things that might happen is like inviting the שטן to make them happen. That is why saying 'many will drink' is not allowed: it speaks about future deaths.

keyTerms.meaning: A person should not 'open his mouth' to the שטן, meaning not speak of possible disasters
And so it was taught in the name of

steps.whyThisMatters: This idea of not 'opening your mouth to the שטן' is a well-known principle that guides how people speak about sad or dangerous things.

phrases.english: As Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish said,
and so it was taught in the name of Rabbi Yosei:

phrases.aramaic: לְעוֹלָם אַל יִפְתַּח אָדָם פִּיו לַשָּׂטָן.
phrases.english: A person should never open his mouth to the Satan.
phrases.notes: He means: don't talk about bad things that could happen, because it is like giving the שטן an opening.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives the reason behind אביי's wording rule.
steps.raayaObject: אביי's rule against saying 'many will drink'
steps.raayaSupportSource: The teaching of ריש לקיש and רבי יוסי: never open your mouth to the שטן

steps.title: The פסוק: Comparing Yourself to סדום
steps.stepSummary: רב יוסף finds a פסוק source: ישראל said 'we were almost like סדום,' and right away the נביא called them 'rulers of סדום.'
steps.simpleTranslation: רב יוסף said: What is the פסוק for this? 'We were almost like סדום, we were like עמורה.' And what did the נביא answer them? 'Hear the word of ה׳, rulers of סדום...'
steps.whatsHappening: רב יוסף brings a פסוק to prove that what a person says about himself can come true.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the first פסוק the people compare themselves to סדום. In the very next פסוק the נביא calls them 'rulers of סדום.' Their own words were used against them, which shows the danger of speaking bad things about yourself.
steps.whatToRemember: Speaking about bad things, even about yourself, can 'open a door' for them to happen. The proof: ישראל compared themselves to סדום and were immediately called 'rulers of סדום.'

phrases.english: Rav Yosef said: What is the verse?
"We were almost like Sodom, we were like Gomorrah."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 1:9

phrases.english: What did [the prophet] answer them?
"Hear the word of ה׳, rulers of Sodom, etc."
phrases.notes: ישעיהו 1:10. Right after they compared themselves to סדום, they were called by that name.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a פסוק source for the rule 'never open your mouth to the שטן.'
steps.raayaObject: The rule that one should not open his mouth to the שטן
steps.raayaSupportSource: ישעיהו 1:9-10: they compared themselves to סדום and were then called 'rulers of סדום'

steps.title: A Blessing for Those Who Come to Comfort
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks יהודה בר נחמני to say words for the comforters, and he blesses them as doers of kindness, ending 'משלם הגמול.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Stand up and say something for the people comforting the mourners. He began: 'Our brothers, doers of kindness, children of doers of kindness, who hold on to the covenant of אברהם אבינו (as it says: "For I know him, that he will command his children..."). Our brothers, may the Master of reward pay you your reward. Blessed are You, Who pays reward.'
steps.whatsHappening: The story goes on with a third request from ריש לקיש. This time יהודה בר נחמני says a blessing for the people who came to comfort.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier he praised ה׳ and spoke to the mourners. Now he turns to the comforters. He praises their kindness as something passed down from אברהם, and asks ה׳ to reward them.

keyTerms.meaning: People who do acts of kindness

phrases.english: He said to him: Stand, say something
phrases.notes: ריש לקיש is again talking to יהודה בר נחמני, like in the last steps.

phrases.english: about those who comfort the mourners.
He began and said:
"Our brothers, doers of kindness,
sons of doers of kindness,
who hold firmly to the covenant of Abraham our father
(as it says: 'For I know him,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the words in round brackets.

phrases.aramaic: לְמַעַן אֲשֶׁר יְצַוֶּה אֶת בָּנָיו וְגוֹ׳׳).
phrases.english: that he will command his children, etc.').
phrases.notes: בראשית 18:19

phrases.aramaic: אַחֵינוּ, בַּעַל הַגְּמוּל יְשַׁלֵּם לָכֶם גְּמוּלְכֶם.
phrases.english: Our brothers, may the Master of reward pay you your reward.
Blessed are You, Who pays reward."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: קוּם אֵימָא מִלְּתָא כְּנֶגֶד מְנַחֲמֵי אֲבֵלִים
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Returns to the story after the side discussion in steps 15-17. After words about ה׳ (step 13) and the mourners (step 14), ריש לקיש now asks for words for the comforters.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The comforters are blessed as doers of kindness following אברהם, with a closing blessing 'משלם הגמול.'

steps.title: A Prayer for All of Israel
steps.stepSummary: ריש לקיש asks for words for all of ישראל, and יהודה בר נחמני prays that ה׳ save the nation from every kind of disaster, ending 'עוצר המגפה.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Stand up and say something for all of ישראל. He began: 'Master of the worlds, redeem and save, rescue and help Your people ישראל from plague, sword, plunder, blight, mildew, and every kind of disaster that bursts into the world. Before we call, You will answer. Blessed are You, Who stops the plague.'
steps.whatsHappening: This is the fourth and last request in the story. Now the blessing is for the whole Jewish people.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The circle grows wider: ה׳, the mourners, the comforters, and now all of ישראל. Because a death happened, he asks ה׳ to stop all disasters for everyone. He ends with 'Who stops the plague.'
steps.whatToRemember: In this story, four blessings are said in the house of mourning: praise of ה׳ (מחיה המתים), comfort for the mourners (מנחם אבלים), a blessing for the comforters (משלם הגמול), and a prayer for all ישראל (עוצר המגפה).

phrases.english: He said to him: Stand, say something
about all of Israel.
He began and said:
"Master of the worlds, redeem and save,
rescue, deliver Your people Israel
from plague and from the sword

phrases.aramaic: וּמִן הַבִּיזָּה וּמִן הַשִּׁדָּפוֹן וּמִן הַיֵּרָקוֹן
phrases.english: and from plunder, and from blight, and from mildew
and from all kinds of disasters
that suddenly burst out and come to the world.
Before we call, You will answer.
Blessed are You, Who stops the plague."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: קוּם אֵימָא מִלְּתָא כְּנֶגֶד כׇּל יִשְׂרָאֵל
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The last of the four requests in the story. It widens from the comforters to all of ישראל.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A prayer for all ישראל to be saved from disasters, ending 'עוצר המגפה.'

steps.title: Ten Cups of Wine in the House of Mourning
steps.stepSummary: עולא (or a ברייתא) teaches that חכמים set up ten cups of wine in the house of mourning: three before the meal, three during, and four after, one for each ברכה of ברכת המזון.
steps.simpleTranslation: עולא said, and some say it was taught in a ברייתא: חכמים set up ten cups in the house of mourning. Three before the meal, to open up his appetite. Three during the meal, to help the food digest. Four after the meal: one for 'הזן,' one for the blessing of the land, one for 'בונה ירושלים,' and one for 'הטוב והמטיב.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to a new teaching that is still about the house of mourning: ten cups of wine that חכמים set up there.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ten cups are split by when they are drunk. The first six help the mourner eat and digest. The last four each go with one of the four ברכות of ברכת המזון.

keyTerms.meaning: A ברייתא (a teaching from the time of the תנאים that is not in the משנה)
The חכמים set up (a rabbinic enactment)

steps.confusionAlert: The last four cups are not extra ברכות. Each cup just goes with one of the four regular ברכות of ברכת המזון.

phrases.english: Ulla said,
and some say it was taught in a baraita:

phrases.aramaic: עֲשָׂרָה כּוֹסוֹת תִּקְּנוּ חֲכָמִים בְּבֵית הָאֵבֶל:
phrases.english: The Sages set up ten cups in the house of mourning:
three before the meal,
in order to open up his insides.
phrases.notes: He means: to give the mourner an appetite.

phrases.english: Three during the meal,
in order to soak the food in his insides.
And four after the meal:
one for "Who feeds",
and one for the blessing of the land,
and one for "Who builds Jerusalem",
and one for "Who is good and does good."

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר עוּלָּא, וְאָמְרִי לַהּ בְּמַתְנִיתָא תָּנָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Starts a new teaching on the same topic, the house of mourning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Ten cups in the house of mourning: three before the meal, three during, and four after, one for each ברכה of ברכת המזון.

steps.title: Four extra cups are added, then removed
steps.stepSummary: חכמים added four more cups to the ten, honoring the city attendants, the city leaders, the בית המקדש, and רבן גמליאל. When people began getting drunk, they went back to the original ten.
steps.simpleTranslation: They added four more cups: one for the city attendants, one for the city leaders, one for the בית המקדש, and one for רבן גמליאל. People started drinking and getting drunk, so חכמים put things back the way they were.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא continues the teaching about the ten cups in a house of mourning. It says four more cups were once added, but the addition was later cancelled.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Each new cup honored someone connected to mourning: the people who handled burials, the leaders who paid for burying the poor, the destroyed בית המקדש, and רבן גמליאל. Fourteen cups led people to get drunk, so the תקנה was rolled back to ten.

keyTerms.meaning: The city attendants, who helped with burials and community needs
The city leaders, who paid community costs such as burying the poor
They returned the matter to its old way

steps.confusionAlert: The final number is ten cups, not fourteen. The four extra cups were added and then taken away again.

phrases.english: They added four to them:
phrases.notes: "Them" means the ten cups from the previous step.

phrases.english: one for the attendants of the city,
and one for the leaders of the city,
and one for the Temple,
and one for Rabban Gamliel.
They began drinking and getting drunk,
phrases.notes: Some versions leave out the word in round brackets. The meaning stays the same.

phrases.english: so they returned the matter to its old way.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the ten-cups teaching from Step 20 and tells how it was briefly expanded.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Four cups were added, but because of drunkenness the number went back to ten.

steps.title: Why is there a cup for רבן גמליאל?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא asks what רבן גמליאל has to do with a house of mourning.
steps.simpleTranslation: What is the cup for רבן גמליאל about?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא asks a short question about the last of the four extra cups. It is setting up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: It is easy to see why the attendants, the leaders, and the בית המקדש connect to mourning. It is not clear why one particular תנא would have a cup in his honor.

phrases.english: What is the matter of Rabban Gamliel?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Asks about one detail from Step 21.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why רבן גמליאל is honored with a cup in a house of mourning.

steps.title: רבן גמליאל made burials simple
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא explains that burials had become so costly that relatives abandoned the dead and ran away. רבן גמליאל asked to be buried in simple linen, and everyone followed his example.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: At first, burying a dead person was harder on his relatives than the death itself, so much that they would leave the body and run away. Then רבן גמליאל acted humbly and was buried in linen garments, and all the people followed him and were buried in linen.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא answers the question by quoting a ברייתא. רבן גמליאל ended the costly burial customs that were crushing families.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Burial clothes had become so expensive that the cost was harder on families than losing their relative, and some simply fled. By choosing plain linen for himself, רבן גמליאל let everyone do the same without shame. That is why mourners drink a cup in his honor.

keyTerms.meaning: Taking out the dead for burial, including its costs
He treated himself lightly, acting humbly

steps.whyThisMatters: This is the source for the custom of burying everyone in simple shrouds, so the poor are not shamed and families are not ruined by costs.

phrases.english: As it was taught: At first,
the taking out of the dead was hard on his relatives
phrases.notes: "Taking out" here means the funeral and its costs, especially the fancy burial clothes.

phrases.english: more than his death,
until they would leave him and flee.
Until Rabban Gamliel came
and acted humbly with himself,
and they took him out in linen garments.
And all the people followed his practice
to take out the dead in linen garments.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 22.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: רבן גמליאל ended expensive burials by choosing simple linen for himself, which saved families from ruin.

steps.title: Today people use even cheaper cloth
steps.stepSummary: רב פפא says that in his time people bury the dead even in rough cloth worth just one זוז.
steps.simpleTranslation: רב פפא said: Nowadays everyone does it even with rough cloth worth one זוז.
steps.whatsHappening: רב פפא adds how the custom looks in his own day. Burials became even simpler and cheaper than linen.
steps.deeperAnalysis: רבן גמליאל's change kept spreading. By רב פפא's time, even very cheap rough cloth was normal for burial, so nobody needed to feel ashamed.
steps.whatToRemember: The cup for רבן גמליאל thanks him for making burial simple and affordable, a custom that grew even simpler over time.

phrases.english: Rav Pappa said:
And nowadays everyone is accustomed
even to rough cloth worth a zuz.
phrases.notes: A זוז is a small coin, so this is very cheap material.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַר רַב פָּפָּא: וְהָאִידָּנָא נְהוּג עָלְמָא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Adds the later practice to the ברייתא of Step 23.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Today people bury the dead even in cheap rough cloth.

steps.title: רבי אלעזר begins a new statement
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא introduces a teaching from רבי אלעזר, which continues on the next amud.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said:
steps.whatsHappening: This line only names the speaker of the next teaching. The גמרא is setting up a new statement that comes right after this.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The discussion of רבן גמליאל and burial customs is finished. A new statement from רבי אלעזר is about to start, and its content appears in the next lines.

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Introduces a new statement after the רבן גמליאל discussion ends.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The content of רבי אלעזר's statement comes on the next amud.
